title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with new partnerships and technological advancements, while funding for resilience continues to be a hot topic. Meanwhile, the specter of hypersonic delays looms large, reminding us that not all progress is linear.

themes.title: New Partnerships Emerge
themes.body: Orbes' unveiling of Exo-ORB alongside a deal with Symphony Space signals a growing trend of collaboration in the sector. Such partnerships may be key to navigating the complexities of modern space endeavors.

themes.title: Funding for Resilience Grows
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4B boost for space resilience highlights a strategic pivot towards safeguarding assets in an increasingly contested environment. This funding could reshape priorities for both established players and newcomers.

themes.title: Tech Innovations Continue
themes.body: Intel's new chip for space computing and Sierra Space's Dream Chaser DoD variant clearing critical design review showcase the relentless march of technological progress. These developments underscore the importance of innovation in maintaining competitive advantage.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hiccups Persist
themes.body: The repeated delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests serve as a sobering reminder that not all advancements are immediate. This ongoing struggle could have implications for defense strategies and funding allocations.
